claim.pdf_says: FUNCTION  LENGTH  ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] )  -- with FUNCTION, LENGTH and PHYSICAL each UNDERLINED in the printed general format (5.2.6.2: an underlined word is a required word).
claim.markdown_says:
```
FUNCTION LENGTH ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] )
```  -- plain fenced code, no underline markup. The same loss occurs in every general format on this batch except 15.58.2 and 15.59.2: 15.51.2 (p905, bare paragraph text), 15.52.2 (p906, inline backticks), 15.53.2 (p907, bare paragraph text), 15.54.2 (p908, fenced code), 15.55.2 (p909, inline backticks), 15.56.2 (p910, inline backticks), 15.57.2 (p911, bare paragraph text).
claim.why_it_matters: The transcription elsewhere DOES carry the standard's underlining as <u>...</u> (97 occurrences, including 15.58.2 '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC</u> ( argument-1 )' on p912 and 15.59.2 '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>MAX</u> ( { argument-1 } ... )' on p914 in this very batch). Dropping it on the neighbouring formats loses the required-word marking that 5.2.6.2 makes normative, and the four different renderings used within ten pages (fenced code / inline code / bare paragraph / <u>) make the general-format blocks non-uniform and unreliable to machine-extract. No alternative-selection information is lost on these particular pages, because every uppercase word in each of these formats is underlined in the PDF; hence cosmetic rather than normative.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on both sources, with two corrections to the claim's rationale.

PDF side (independently verified): rendered specs PDF page 903 (printed page 873, 15.50 LENGTH function) at 300 dpi and cropped the 15.50.2 General format line to ~8x magnification. I see three separate horizontal rules under exactly three words: FUNCTION, LENGTH, and PHYSICAL. The rules stop cleanly at each word boundary -- 'argument-1', the parentheses '( )' and the brackets '[ ]' carry no rule. So the printed format is FUNCTION LENGTH ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] ) with those three words underlined, exactly as claimed.

Markdown side (independently verified): specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 36121-36126 render 15.50.2 as a bare fenced code block containing the single line 'FUNCTION LENGTH ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] )' with no <u> markup, no bold, and no accompanying figure note. The character sequence is identical; only the underline information is absent. This is not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation or page-break furniture -- the text is on one line in both sources.

Not merely formatting: the standard makes underlining normative notation, so its loss is a content loss in principle rather than typography. Verified verbatim in the transcription itself -- 5.2.2 Keywords: 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword'; 5.2.3 Optional words: 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity'; restated at 8.3.2.4.2 Required words ('1) Keywords. Within each format, such words are uppercase and underlined') and 8.3.2.4.3 Optional words ('uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format'). Underlining is therefore the sole device distinguishing a required keyword from an omissible noise word.

Neighbouring-format survey (independently verified): I read all ten sections 15.50.2-15.59.2 in specs/ISO_COBOL.md and every rendering is exactly as the claim describes -- fenced code (15.50.2, 15.54.2), bare paragraph (15.51.2, 15.53.2, 15.57.2), inline backticks (15.52.2, 15.55.2, 15.56.2), and <u> markup only at 15.58.2 ('<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC</u> ( argument-1 )') and 15.59.2 ('<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>MAX</u> ( { argument-1 } ... )'). The claim misquotes neither source.

Severity 'cosmetic' is correct and I corroborated its stated rationale rather than taking it on trust: I additionally rendered page 911 (15.57.2 LOWER-CASE) and confirmed that FUNCTION, LOWER-CASE and LOCALE are all three underlined, so no optional-word survives un-underlined anywhere in this batch and no alternative-selection information is actually lost. On p903 specifically, PHYSICAL stands alone inside brackets, so reading it as an optional word would make the bracket vacuous -- the required-word status is recoverable by inspection.

Two corrections are required and are recorded in corrected_description: the claim cites the wrong section, and it mischaracterises the transcription's underline convention.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, but the rationale needs two fixes.

(1) WRONG CITATION. The claim twice attributes the normative force of underlining to '5.2.6.2'. Section 5.2.6.2 is 'Brackets' and says nothing about underlining -- it defines the meaning of '[ ]'. The correct citations are 5.2.2 (Keywords -- 'shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required...') and 5.2.3 (Optional words -- 'shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats'), restated normatively at 8.3.2.4.2 (Required words) and 8.3.2.4.3 (Optional words). Any ledger entry or fix derived from this finding must cite 5.2.2 / 5.2.3 (and 8.3.2.4.2 / 8.3.2.4.3), not 5.2.6.2.

(2) MISCHARACTERISED CONVENTION, AND THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN CLAIMED. The claim frames inline <u>...</u> as the transcription's established convention that p903 fails to follow. It is not the dominant device. The transcription's principal mechanism for preserving underline information is a prose 'Figure notes' block: 225 such blocks exist, 213 of which explicitly enumerate which words are underlined and which are not -- and they are careful enough to flag ISO's own typesetting defects (e.g. the LISTING directive note records that 'ON' is printed without an underline although the general rules treat it as specifiable). Inline <u> is the secondary device at 97 lines / 156 tags. Measured against 360 'General format' headings in the file, the majority of general formats carry NEITHER device, and only 6 Figure-notes blocks fall in the clause-15 intrinsic-function range at all. So there are five renderings in circulation, not four (fenced code / inline code / bare paragraph / <u> / figure-note prose), and the non-uniformity is a document-wide property of the transcription rather than an anomaly local to pages 903-914. The p903 entry should be treated as one instance of a systemic class, and any remediation should pick ONE canonical representation for general formats and apply it globally.

(3) SEVERITY CONFIRMED, WITH A CAVEAT ON THE CLASS. 'Cosmetic' is right for p903 and for this batch: I verified on p903 (FUNCTION, LENGTH, PHYSICAL) and p911 (FUNCTION, LOWER-CASE, LOCALE) that every uppercase word in these formats is underlined, so no required/optional distinction is destroyed here. But the defect class is NORMATIVE, not cosmetic, wherever a printed format mixes underlined and non-underlined uppercase words -- the transcription's own figure notes document exactly such cases (SOURCE FORMAT IS FIXED, where FORMAT and IS are not underlined; the FLAG-02, LISTING, PROPAGATE, TURN and figurative-constant formats). In a plain-text rendering of those, an omissible noise word is indistinguishable from a required keyword, which would directly mislead a compiler implementation. p903 simply happens not to be such a case.
